name: Vantage

profile.reading: This is one of three data center buildings on Vantage Data Centers' New Albany, Ohio campus at 3325 Horizon Court, in Licking/Franklin County's New Albany International Business Park, one of the largest concentrations of hyperscale data center construction in the eastern United States. The New Albany park has drawn Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Vantage, pulled by AEP Ohio's transmission capacity, the state's data center sales-and-use-tax exemption program, and local economic-development incentives negotiated with New Albany and Licking County. Vantage's own campus materials describe the site as roughly 70 acres with about 1.5 million square feet planned across three two-story buildings, each stated at approximately 64 megawatts of critical IT capacity, for a total campus capacity near 192 megawatts once all phases are complete; Vantage's page does not assign individual names, building numbers, or separately confirmed square-footage figures to each of the three structures beyond this uniform per-building description, so an even division of the 1.5 million total (approximately 500,000 square feet per building) is this profile's derived estimate rather than an operator-confirmed number for this specific building. Vantage has stated the first building was slated to reach operational status in December 2025, with additional phases continuing through 2028. Power is supplied end-to-end at 480 volts, with N+1 electrical and N+2 mechanical redundancy per Vantage's standard design, and each building is targeted for LEED Silver certification. Vantage Data Centers, headquartered in Denver, is backed by DigitalBridge and Silver Lake, which committed $6.4 billion in fresh capital to the company in January 2024; Ohio's rapid data center buildout, concentrated heavily in New Albany and neighboring Licking County communities, has become a subject of statewide debate over electricity rate impacts on residential customers, prompting AEP Ohio to propose a distinct large-load tariff class for data centers before the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio.
